title: Air India Adds Wood-Fired Pizzas to In-Flight Menu on Select US-India Routes
excerpt: The stone-baked option is now available in Economy and Premium Economy on five North America routes as part of the airline's ongoing dining overhaul.
body:
• Air India has introduced stone-baked, wood-fired pizzas on select long-haul flights between North America and India, available in Economy and Premium Economy cabins.
  • The pizzas are currently served on routes connecting JFK, SFO, Newark, Toronto, and Vancouver with Delhi and Mumbai.
  • The addition is part of a broader international menu refresh under Air India's transformation programme, which introduced a revamped global menu in November 2025.

Air India has added freshly stone-baked, wood-fired pizzas to the in-flight menu on select long-haul routes between North America and India, marking the latest step in the airline's ongoing effort to overhaul its onboard dining experience.

The pizzas are now available in Economy and Premium Economy cabins on five routes: New York JFK to Delhi, San Francisco to Delhi, Newark to Mumbai, Toronto to Delhi, and Vancouver to Delhi. Air India announced the new offering through its official newsroom social media account, according to Safari India.

Part of a Bigger Menu Overhaul

"An Airline in the Middle of a Makeover The food upgrade is one of many visible changes Air India is making as part of its multi-billion-dollar transformation under Tata Group ownership."

The pizza addition builds on a comprehensive menu refresh that Air India rolled out in November 2025 under the direction of Chef Sandeep Kalra. That revamp introduced regional Indian signatures — from Awadhi thalis and South Indian platters to Rajasthani besan chilla — alongside international options like Korean bibimbap and Japanese teppanyaki bowls across First, Business, and Premium Economy classes.

The latest addition targets passengers in Economy and Premium Economy, where food options on long-haul flights have historically been more limited. Stone-baked pizza, which retains its texture better at altitude than many reheated dishes, is a practical choice for the 15- to 17-hour flights connecting North American cities with the Indian subcontinent.

An Airline in the Middle of a Makeover

The food upgrade is one of many visible changes Air India is making as part of its multi-billion-dollar transformation under Tata Group ownership. Since taking over the former state-owned carrier in January 2022, Tata has been refurbishing the existing fleet, upgrading cabins, retraining cabin crew, and revamping everything from the airline's booking systems to its brand identity.

The transformation has been costly — Air India and its budget subsidiary Air India Express posted combined losses of $2.33 billion in the fiscal year ended March 2026. But service-level improvements like the menu overhaul are designed to rebuild the airline's reputation with passengers who have long complained about dated interiors and uninspired food on what were once flagship routes.

Why It Matters for Diaspora Travelers

For the millions of Indian-Americans and NRIs who fly these US-India routes regularly, in-flight food quality has long been a sore point and a frequent topic of social media commentary. Air India's North American routes — particularly JFK-Delhi and SFO-Delhi — are among the most heavily traveled by the Indian diaspora, making them a natural testing ground for menu experiments. Whether wood-fired pizza at 35,000 feet lives up to its ground-level counterpart remains to be seen, but the gesture signals that Air India is paying attention to the passenger experience, one meal tray at a time.
